impact: Field report (ledger-integrity-protocol, 2026-09-15, provider gemini via failover): Gemini read a test comment naming the mutant it catches (e.g. "M-PANE-WITHOUT-LEDGER opens unconditionally and this fails") as documentation that the test is expected to fail, and returned a major finding recommending test.skip. This is a reviewer-prompt gap, not a caller bug (contrast with the cross-chunk false positive already tracked in ISS-020, which is on the caller/chunking side). Suggested fix: if the bridge prepends reviewer guidance/system instructions, add a line clarifying that a comment naming a mutant ID describes what the test is designed to catch, not an expected failure — this should remove a class of false majors on mutation-tested code.
title: Gemini reviewer flags mutant-naming test comments as a false-positive major asking for test.skip
